newsitem.title: USA: Coast Guard cutter, cargo carrier collide.
newsitem.headline: Coast Guard cutter, cargo carrier collide.

text.p: A Coast Guard cutter was heavily damaged and spilled diesel fuel into the Columbia River when it collided with a cargo ship in heavy fog, officials said Thursday.

The 180-foot (54-metre) cutter Cowslip was heading upriver near the mouth of the Columbia late Wednesday when it scraped the oncoming M.V. Evergrade, a 757-foot (227-metre) container ship on its way to Tokyo, Coast Guard officials said.

The Coast Guard boat sustained heavy damage to its port side and one minor injury. An undetermined amount of diesel fuel was spilled into the river, but the environmental impact was minimal as tides flushed the fuel out to sea from the accident site near Astoria, Ore., the Coast Guard said.
A spokesman for the Coast Guard said visibility was only 20 yards when the two ships collided as they were approaching a bend in the river.
The cargo ship, whose owner was identified as Greencompass Marine, was being detained off the coast while authorities investigated the incident.
It was not known what cargo the Evergrade was carrying.
